What a finding means for you

An inspection is only useful if it ends in a clear decision. These are common findings, and the step that usually follows.

FindingWhat it usually meansUsual next step
Bruised or cracked shinglesHail has broken the granule layer. The shingle still looks fine from the street but ages fast.Repair or replace
A stain on the ceilingWater is getting in, often at flashing, a vent or a worn section. The cause is rarely right above the stain.Repair soon
Ice along the eavesHeat escapes into the attic and melts snow that refreezes at the edge, where it backs up under the shingles.Check ventilation
Missing shingles on a younger roofWind damage on a roof with plenty of life left. A targeted repair is usually enough.Targeted repair
Curling across the whole roofThe roof is near the end of its life. Repairs will keep coming back.Plan a replacement
